##  · DOC1-sftp-confinement — userland/transfer.md: where SFTP and SCP run and how they are confined

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 9

### Userland writer · Question

Event: `ce64ef6f600db5db673eb0ebba4497b0` · 2026-09-26T08:01:42Z

> M3 (files in and out): 'SFTP and SCP inside SSH, confined to the session's capabilities and audited'. No design exists. RECOMMENDATION: sshd only relays the channel's bytes. The SFTP subsystem (and SCP, served as its own protocol) runs as a per-connection process the steward starts inside the session's budget, with exactly the session's namespace and label set (a vault session's transfer is labelled like the vault), so it can reach nothing the session could not; paths resolve through that namespace and `..` is cleaned lexically; no symlink or chmod/chown operation does anything (refused or no-op as File does). Each open-for-write, remove, rename and mkdir is recorded in the audit log with the principal and path. Alternative: serve SFTP from inside the session's Elixir VM with OTP's ssh_sftpd over File (less code, but puts the SSH subsystem parser in the session VM). Until answered the page lists this under Open.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `e088c03cd9c24604074e95c10bb40e58` · 2026-09-26T08:04:32Z

> Architect ruling, M3 (files in and out), for servers/sshd.md and userland/file-transfer.md. The RECOMMENDATION's structure is adopted, with one correction from a settled rule and five sharpenings.
> 
> CORRECTION: labelled (vault) sessions get no SFTP or SCP. The settled containment rule (legacy CONTAINMENT, Sessions and vaults) makes sshd the one sink cleared for a label only on the owner's pty channel, 'with no forwarding, no subsystems and no exec'. Vault input enters by an audited steward push, and output leaves by declassification. The brief's 'confined to the session's capabilities' does not reopen that. So a subsystem request on a labelled channel is refused, and the page says why. Opening vault transfers would be a new label sink and a genuine owner decision; nobody has asked for it.
> 
> DESIGN (unlabelled sessions):
> 1. sshd relays bytes only. On a `subsystem sftp` request it asks the steward to start the transfer server for that session and pipes the channel to it, as it does /dev/cons. sshd never parses SFTP.
> 2. The transfer server is a small native Rust program. The steward starts one per channel, in a budget carved from the session's. It gets only the session's file binds: no /net, no /dev/cons, no powerbox, no budget or process handles. That is narrower than the session, as TENETS allows. An SFTP-only connection gets a session budget as a login does, with the transfer server instead of beamlet.
> 3. Confinement is by capability, not by path strings. The server holds namespace handles and nothing else, so no path, however written, reaches anything outside. `..` at the namespace root stays at the root (walk semantics). Lexical cleaning is for predictable names, not a wall.
> 4. Unsupported operations fail visibly. SYMLINK, READLINK and LINK get SSH_FX_OP_UNSUPPORTED. SETSTAT honours size (truncate), and mtime if fsd stores it; mode, uid and gid get OP_UNSUPPORTED rather than a silent no-op. No silent success.
> 5. SCP is served only as SFTP. OpenSSH 9+ scp uses the SFTP protocol by default. Legacy scp (`scp -O`, an exec of `scp -t/-f`) is refused, since Redoubt has no exec and no shell to run it, which saves a second protocol parser. The page tells old clients to use `sftp` or `scp -s`.
> 6. Audit. One record per operation, not per byte: every open (read and write, since M3 is files in AND out), close with the byte count, remove, rename, mkdir, rmdir and setstat. Each goes through the steward's audit path, signed as every audit record is. The principal and labels in a record come from the badge the steward minted for the server, never from the server's own claim, so the server cannot forge whose transfer it was.
> 
> WHY NOT ssh_sftpd in the session VM: the principal controls their own VM, so audit records emitted there could be skipped at will. It would also need a full VM per SFTP-only connection, and ssh_sftpd is built for OTP's ssh daemon, not a raw byte pipe.
> 
> RESIDUAL, stated plainly: the audit is accountability, not a wall. A principal who compromises their own transfer server with crafted input holds only their session's file capabilities, which they already had. They could suppress their own records, and they could anyway move data out unaudited through the pty. Open: fsd-side auditing of transfer handles, only if audit must survive a compromised transfer server.
> 
> TESTS for M3 (files in and out):
> - a path-escape suite (`..`, absolute paths, long and odd names) reaches only the session's binds;
> - symlink, chmod and chown are refused;
> - `scp -O` is refused;
> - a subsystem request on a vault channel is refused;
> - every operation yields exactly one signed audit record with the right principal;
> - a second principal's files are unreachable.

> cc: DOC1-sftp-confinement answered.
> - Vault (labelled) sessions get no SFTP or SCP, per the settled containment rule (the owner's pty channel only: no subsystems, no exec, no forwarding). Opening them would be a new owner decision.
> - Unlabelled sessions: sshd relays only; the steward starts a per-channel native Rust transfer server in a budget carved from the session, holding only the session's file binds.
> - Confinement is by capability. Symlink, chmod and chown fail visibly. SCP is served only as SFTP (`scp -O` is refused).
> - Every operation is audited through the steward, with the principal taken from the badge. Stated residual: the audit is accountability, not a wall.
> - One Open item: fsd-side auditing.

Event: `8564dabb2bc78d911c1c8c1098478749` · 2026-09-26T08:14:21Z

> The DOC1 brief conflicts with itself on milestones. M3 (files in and out) says SFTP/SCP transfers are "audited", but "the audit log exists" is listed under M4 (self-hosted development). Something has to record M3's transfers.
> 
> RECOMMENDATION: move the minimal audit log into M3. That means steward-written, append-only records, each signed through keyd's audit purpose (already built in keyd), with the settled record format: labels, principal chain, read under the label check. M3 records transfers only. M4 extends the same log to every steward action (grants, leases, agents, approvals). Chaining the records and the operator's verifier tool stay in M5 (persist, install, share), with log retention.
> 
> ALTERNATIVES:
> (a) Keep the audit log wholly in M4, and M3 ships transfers with the audit hook but no log. That's simpler for M3, but M3's "audited" would be false until M4.
> (b) Move the whole audit log, including every steward action, into M3. That makes M3 bigger for little gain, since the other audited actions (agent leases and grants) mostly arrive in M4.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `e94a67d7de7e189c3b853c819b086f78` · 2026-09-26T08:14:30Z

> Two parts.
> 
> WHICH OPERATIONS: already ruled on this thread (DESIGN point 6), and it supersedes the recommendation's list. One record per operation: every open (read and write, since M3 is files in AND out), close with the byte count, remove, rename, mkdir, rmdir and setstat. 'Reads per file in vault sessions' does not arise: labelled (vault) sessions get no SFTP or SCP at all (the CORRECTION on this thread, from the settled containment rule).
> 
> WHICH MILESTONE RECORDS THEM: the brief conflicts with itself (M3 'audited', while M4 has 'the audit log exists'). Moving scope between milestones is the owner's call, so I've sent a decision_request on this thread. The recommendation:
> - The minimal audit log moves into M3: steward-written, append-only, recording transfers only.
> - M4 extends the same log to every steward action.
> - Chaining and the verifier stay in M5 (persist, install, share), with retention.
> One amendment to your version: the minimal log is not unsigned. Per-record signatures are the settled design (legacy CONTAINMENT, steward: each record is signed through keyd's audit purpose over 'redoubt.audit.v1\0' || len || record). keyd's audit purpose is built today, so M3 signs from the start. What waits for M5 is chaining (catching dropped or reordered records) and the verifier tool.
> Until the owner answers, the page keeps the milestone placement under Open and states the recommendation. The operation list is decided.
